title: Embedding/rerank throughput drop and quality drift during quantization rollout
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Summary:
On 2025-02-18 we observed a sustained throughput drop and increased tail latency for the embeddings + rerank endpoint (prod, region us-west-2) coinciding with a downstream quality regression in reranking scores for a subset of customer traffic. The incident lasted ~6 hours and affected ~12% of requests to the rerank path (peak error/latency window 14:05-20:00 UTC). Production alerts triggered by autoscaler oscillation and per-shard OOMs.

Impact:
- Increased median latency from 85ms to 360ms for embedded->rerank end-to-end flows for impacted shards.
- Tail P99 latency spikes to ~1.8s for affected requests.
- Rerank quality drift: candidate ordering changes measured as a 7.4% drop in NDCG@10 on internal evaluation set for traffic routed to canaries.
- Customers: several PLG customers reported elevated error rates in dashboards and automated tests (support tickets opened).

Timeline (key events):
- 2025-02-18 13:30 UTC: Canary rollout of quantization microkernel change (int8 path) and tokenizer library upgrade (tokenizer v2.14) launched to 10% of rerank allocation.
- 2025-02-18 13:58 UTC: Autoscaler reports growing pod churn; early alerts at 14:05 UTC for elevated pod restarts in embedding workers.
- 2025-02-18 14:30 UTC: Monitoring shows per-request GPU memory usage increase (~18%) on canary hosts; KV cache hit rate reduced on these hosts due to cache thrash.
- 2025-02-18 15:05 UTC: Canary traffic shows NDCG@10 regression compared to baseline; routing policy automatically increased traffic to fallback CPU workers, causing capacity imbalance.
- 2025-02-18 16:00 UTC: Engineering rollback of the quantization kernel (PR #4721) for canaries completed; tokenization change retained for now.
- 2025-02-18 17:15 UTC: Autoscaler dwell timers adjusted and aggressive eviction thresholds relaxed as emergency mitigation.
- 2025-02-18 19:10 UTC: Full rollback to pre-change runtime configuration (quantization off, tokenizer pinned) completed; system stabilized by 20:00 UTC.

Root cause analysis (why it happened):
Multiple interacting changes and gaps in canary testing led to the outage:
1) Quantization microkernel change (float16 -> int8 path) introduced an allocation pattern that increased temporary GPU scratch memory by ~15-20% for typical batch sizes we see on rerank workloads. This was not caught in microbenchmarks because local tests used smaller synthetic batches.
2) Tokenizer v2.14 introduced a subtle change in pre-tokenization normalization which increased average token count for short inputs by ~6%. More tokens combined with increased scratch memory pushed several pods over OOM thresholds under normal load.
3) Autoscaler configuration had conservative cooldown and tight eviction thresholds tuned for cost; when pods exhibited transient higher memory the autoscaler aggressively killed and recreated capacity which caused cache cold starts and cascading latency increases.
4) Canary sampling was limited to 10% host-level routing but did not include realistic long-tail query shapes or peak burst windows; our canary load generator used average-length prompts and missed the tokenization-induced length shift.

Contributing process gaps:
- Lack of end-to-end canary scenarios that exercise realistic token length distribution and batch coalescing behavior.
- No GPU-memory regression gate in CI for the quantization microkernel changes.
- Autoscaler policies lacked a soft-fail mode that would prioritize graceful degradation over immediate pod eviction.

Mitigations taken (short-term during incident):
- Immediate rollback of quantization microkernel to restore memory profile (PR #4721 reverted).
- Pin tokenizer to prior stable version (tokenizer v2.13) while we analyzed drift.
- Temporarily widened autoscaler thresholds and increased cooldown to avoid thrash.
- Opened a support bulletin and marked impacted customers; provided a timeline and mitigation steps.

Permanent fixes and follow-ups (owner assignments included):
1) Add GPU-memory regression tests to PR gating for quant kernel changes (owner: Maya Chen, ENG-37455, due 2025-03-07).
2) Extend canary harness to replay production traces (token length distribution, burst profiles) and include rerank scoring checks (owner: Liam O'Connor, ENG-37478, due 2025-03-14).
3) Implement autoscaler soft-fail mode: prefer traffic shedding and route-based fallback over aggressive pod kills (owner: Diego Alvarez, ENG-37510, due 2025-04-01).
4) Create a preflight model-fidelity check comparing NDCG and embedding cosine drift on sampled canary traffic before enabling quantization (owner: Elena Grigorev, ENG-37522, due 2025-03-21).
5) Improve observability: surfaced per-kernel scratch allocations, per-pod token-length histogram, and rerank-quality deltas in the console (owner: Priya Raman, ENG-37540, due 2025-03-28).

Metrics and verification plan:
- Add a dashboard that tracks mean GPU scratch allocation per-request, per-kernel, and a rolling NDCG delta for canary vs baseline.
- Verification criteria for re-enabling quantization: no >3% increase in avg GPU scratch in 72h of canary traffic and NDCG@10 within ±1% on replayed production trace.

Related artifacts and links:
- Revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4727
- Hotfix PR (autoscaler cooldown): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1012
- Incident dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/incident-2025-02-18
- Support thread: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/INC-1298
- Canary harness issue: ENG-37478

Lessons learned (summary):
- Kernel-level optimizations must include realistic memory-profile gating; microbenchmarks alone are insufficient.
- Canary traffic needs to faithfully represent production tokenization patterns and burstiness for embedding/rerank workloads.
- Autoscaler policies should prefer graceful capacity degradation and provide a backoff window before destructive actions.

Owners and reviewers:
- Incident lead: Diego Alvarez (assignee)
- Root cause analysis lead: Maya Chen
- Quality verification owner: Elena Grigorev
- Platform reviewer: Liam O'Connor

Status: All emergency mitigations implemented and validated. Work is in progress on the permanent follow-ups listed above. Re-enabling quantization will be gated by the new verification criteria and the extended canary harness.
